column1: # replay-hold.tsv -- the bytes a skirmish recording's stream holds between refreshes
# (tagpu_reclossy.c). tools/replay-hold-gen.py says what the columns mean and generates
# inc/tagpu_rechold.h from this file; the build fails when the two disagree. Each recording carries
# the masks it was written with and this file's SHA-256 (RT_HOLD), so a change here never orphans
# WHAT A ROW MEANS. A held byte is written into the stream only when its record is written for a
# byte that is not held -- a unit's delta, an order list sent whole -- and at every refresh, where
# the stream's world equals the writer's exact copy byte for byte; between two refreshes it keeps
# a value the engine produced for the same unit or list since the last. Every byte no row names is
# exact at every iteration. A takeover or a fork starts only at a refresh, so it never starts from
# A ROW IS A LOOSENING, and adding one is the owner's decision (CLAUDE.md, *Loosening is the
# owner's decision*). A row names the readers of its bytes that run on a playback host, `-` for
# none, and its evidence: DISASSEMBLED with the addresses, or MEASURED with the numbers. A reader
# found on a puppet that shows a held byte removes the row.
# NOT COVERED BY CONSTRUCTION: the extra weapons' side slots (weapons 4..N) live outside the unit
# image, in declared tables, which the stream carries exact.
